items.name: 01 Property value jumps when income comes online. A single-family home is worth
items.text: 01 Property value jumps when income comes online. A single-family home is worth what comparable homes nearby sold for. The same lot with producing units is worth its NOI capitalized at market. You're not adding 4 units. You're changing how the entire property gets valued.

items.name: 02 Cash flow from day one. New ADUs in San Diego rent at strong premiums to cons
items.text: 02 Cash flow from day one. New ADUs in San Diego rent at strong premiums to construction cost basis. — even after the new loan service. The original house plus producing units becomes an income-generating asset. Once leased up, the property pays you every month

items.name: 03 Cash-out refinance returns your equity. After lease-up, you refinance at the
items.text: 03 Cash-out refinance returns your equity. After lease-up, you refinance at the new (much higher) appraised value. Your money comes back. The new loan is serviced by your tenants. You're free to redeploy into the next project — or just keep it.

items.name: 04 At exit, you sell a producing asset — not just a house. A property valued on
items.text: 04 At exit, you sell a producing asset — not just a house. A property valued on NOI sells to a different buyer pool — investors, not just families. The build is your option to choose either path. Same lot, fundamentally different exit price.

items.name: 01 Stage 1 — Feasibility. What's actually worth building here, and does it penci
items.text: 01 Stage 1 — Feasibility. What's actually worth building here, and does it pencil? Four sub-activities: (a) market analysis — what units does the submarket want, at what rent; (b) site & engineering feasibility; (c) regulatory feasibility — what your specific lot allows under SB 9, ADU law, Density Bonus, SB 1123; (d) financial feasibility — a development proforma covering hard costs, soft costs, financing, lease-up, and refinance into permanent. Output: a clear go / no-go before you commit a me

items.name: 02 Stage 2 — Design & approvals. Design through three phases: Schematic Design →
items.text: 02 Stage 2 — Design & approvals. Design through three phases: Schematic Design → Design Development → Construction Documents. Running in parallel: pre-application meeting with the City, formal submittal, plan check (multiple correction cycles are normal), permit issuance. I run the meetings, manage the timeline, and translate between the City and the design team — so you don't have to. 3–6 months

items.name: 03 Stage 3 — Financing. For Path A (one ADU), often a HELOC or renovation loan.
items.text: 03 Stage 3 — Financing. For Path A (one ADU), often a HELOC or renovation loan. For Path B and C: a — short-term, variable-rate, disbursed in monthly draws. The construction loan gets paid off by the once the property reaches stabilized occupancy. I structure both, run the underwriting packages, and manage the lender relationship through funding. construction loan permanent loan Concurrentwith design

items.name: 04 Stage 4 — Construction. Mobilization, site work, foundation, framing, MEP rou
items.text: 04 Stage 4 — Construction. Mobilization, site work, foundation, framing, MEP rough-in, inspections, drywall, finishes, final inspections, certificate of occupancy. Monthly draw requests filed with the lender. This is the stage where projects either come in on budget, or they don't. The difference is project management — change-order discipline, draw schedule oversight, weekly site walks. 9–18 months

items.name: 05 Stage 5 — Marketing & leasing. Pre-marketing begins during construction; acti
items.text: 05 Stage 5 — Marketing & leasing. Pre-marketing begins during construction; active leasing starts 60–90 days before certificate of occupancy. Target: — because that's the trigger for the permanent loan to fund. Lease-up speed directly affects total interest cost and project profit. stabilized occupancy (90–95% leased) 60–90 dayspre-C of O

items.name: 06 Stage 6 — Operations, refinance & exit. Once stabilized, the development peri
items.text: 06 Stage 6 — Operations, refinance & exit. Once stabilized, the development period ends and the operating period begins. the permanent loan pays off construction, the cash-out returns your equity, and you hold as a producing asset. if the goal is a one-time gain, the project can be sold to an investor at stabilized value — typically much higher than all-in cost. Refinance: Sell: Hold or Exit

items.name: 01 Tenants pay your mortgage. On a typical San Diego fourplex, the rent from the
items.text: 01 Tenants pay your mortgage. On a typical San Diego fourplex, the rent from the three units you don't live in often covers most of the mortgage, taxes, insurance, and reserves. Your effective housing cost ends up below renting the same unit.

items.name: 02 Equity builds faster. 4× A single-family buyer pays down their loan with one
items.text: 02 Equity builds faster. 4× A single-family buyer pays down their loan with one source: their own income. A multifamily buyer has three or four sources paying down the loan. Same down payment. Substantially more equity built over five years.

items.name: 03 Cash flow, not a money pit. A single-family home costs you money every month
items.text: 03 Cash flow, not a money pit. A single-family home costs you money every month — mortgage, taxes, insurance, repairs, no offsetting income. A well-priced multifamily produces cash flow once stabilized. That difference compounds for decades.

items.name: 04 You exit on NOI — not comps. A house sells on what other houses nearby sold f
items.text: 04 You exit on NOI — not comps. A house sells on what other houses nearby sold for. A multifamily property sells on its NOI capitalized at the local cap rate. — independent of your neighbors. The income you build directly drives what you can sell for

items.name: 01 Strategy session & lender pre-approval. Your goals, timeline, cash, credit. T
items.text: 01 Strategy session & lender pre-approval. Your goals, timeline, cash, credit. Then a multifamily-savvy lender to map your loan products and pre-approval — what you actually qualify for, owner-occupied vs. investor financing, FHA vs. conventional. Most people skip this step and look at properties they can't actually buy. We don't. Week 1

items.name: 02 Targeted San Diego search. Duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes that match your pu
items.text: 02 Targeted San Diego search. Duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes that match your purchasing power and the submarkets that fit your strategy. On-market and off-market. Including small properties with unrealized development upside under — value most agents miss. SB 9 / ADU law Ongoing

items.name: 03 Full proforma on every property worth a second look. The full underwrite — gr
items.text: 03 Full proforma on every property worth a second look. The full underwrite — gross rent through NOI through cash flow through cap rate, cash-on-cash, DSCR, and break-even. Plus a sensitivity table on vacancy, rent growth, and rate shocks. Delivered as a clean one-page summary you can actually read. 24–48 hrper property

items.name: 04 Offer strategy & negotiation. Price, contingencies, due diligence period, fin
items.text: 04 Offer strategy & negotiation. Price, contingencies, due diligence period, financing terms, leaseback if you need it. Coordination with the listing agent, escrow, your lender, the inspector, the appraiser. — not what the seller is asking. The proforma we built becomes the basis for what we'll pay Days 1–14per offer

items.name: 05 Due diligence — verify everything in the proforma. Rent roll audit (tenant by
items.text: 05 Due diligence — verify everything in the proforma. Rent roll audit (tenant by tenant). Lease review (rent, term, deposits, special clauses). Trailing 12 months of seller financials. Property inspection. Permits and code compliance. Every assumption gets verified — or updated. We make decisions on updated numbers, not listing numbers. 14–17 days

items.name: 06 Close — and the model becomes your operating playbook. After close, the profo
items.text: 06 Close — and the model becomes your operating playbook. After close, the proforma becomes your tracking baseline. Year 1 actuals vs. Year 1 model. Where you're outperforming, where you're underperforming, when to refinance, when to start thinking about the next one. You're not a homeowner who happens to have tenants. You're an investor with a plan. Day 0+Repeats

items.name: A. Before the earnest money contract First pass — listing rents, listed expenses
items.text: A. Before the earnest money contract First pass — listing rents, listed expenses, market cap, your loan terms. If it doesn't clear your hurdle rate at Stage 1, we don't write the offer.

items.name: B. Before approaching lenders Updated with verified rent roll, T-12 financials f
items.text: B. Before approaching lenders Updated with verified rent roll, T-12 financials from the seller, refined OpEx assumptions. The version that goes into your lender's underwriting package — and that they will sensitivity-test for DSCR.

items.name: C. Before "going hard" on the contract After due diligence: inspection results,
items.text: C. Before "going hard" on the contract After due diligence: inspection results, lease audits, CapEx surprises. Once you remove contingencies, the deposit is at risk. We don't go hard until the model survives every assumption update due diligence produced.

items.name: D. For an equity raise or partner Stage 5 waterfall — what each side actually re
items.text: D. For an equity raise or partner Stage 5 waterfall — what each side actually receives at base, downside, and upside. Partners deserve to see the math before they wire.

items.name: 01 Investment thesis & acquisition criteria. What are you optimizing for? Cash f
items.text: 01 Investment thesis & acquisition criteria. What are you optimizing for? Cash flow, IRR over a 7-year hold, value-add upside, development play. What submarkets, what unit count, what LTV, what return hurdles. Once the criteria are clear, deal flow becomes filtering — not browsing. Week 1

items.name: 02 Deal sourcing — on-market, off-market, pre-listing. MLS multifamily, off-mark
items.text: 02 Deal sourcing — on-market, off-market, pre-listing. MLS multifamily, off-market relationships, pre-listing inventory through brokerage networks. The bias is toward properties most agents don't bring to scaling investors — small buildings priced for quick sales, owners ready to exit, properties with . hidden development upside Ongoing

items.name: 03 Stage 1 + Stage 2 model on every deal worth considering. Stabilized proforma.
items.text: 03 Stage 1 + Stage 2 model on every deal worth considering. Stabilized proforma. 10-year DCF. Three IRRs. Sensitivity tables. Side-by-side comparison when you're considering more than one. The model goes back to you in a format you can actually read and use. 24–48 hr

items.name: 04 Offer strategy & negotiation. Price, terms, contingencies, due diligence peri
items.text: 04 Offer strategy & negotiation. Price, terms, contingencies, due diligence period, financing structure. Where to be aggressive, where to give in. Coordination with the seller's broker, the lender, escrow. Days 1–14

items.name: 05 Due diligence — verify every assumption in the model. Rent roll audit. Lease
items.text: 05 Due diligence — verify every assumption in the model. Rent roll audit. Lease review. T-12 financials. Service contracts. Property inspection. Title review. Environmental if needed. Each finding either confirms a model assumption or updates it. The model goes back through with the new inputs. 14–17 days

items.name: 06 Close — and the model becomes your asset management baseline. After close, th
items.text: 06 Close — and the model becomes your asset management baseline. After close, the proforma becomes the tracking baseline. Year 1 actuals vs. Year 1 model. Where you're outperforming. Where you're underperforming. The underwriting doesn't end at close. It becomes the operating playbook. Day 0+

items.name: 01 Your lot might be worth more than the house. If your lot is eligible for an S
items.text: 01 Your lot might be worth more than the house. If your lot is eligible for an SB 9 split or a detached ADU, it changes who wants to buy it. Identifying that upside expands your buyer pool and raises your price ceiling. We aren’t just selling a 3-bedroom house — we’re selling a small-scale development opportunity.

items.name: 02 Two buyer pools pay more than one. If the valuation shows your home appeals t
items.text: 02 Two buyer pools pay more than one. If the valuation shows your home appeals to investors or developers, we don’t run one marketing campaign — we run two. The lifestyle of your home goes to families. The hard data, proformas, and development upside go to my network of investors.

items.name: 03 Defensible pricing stops appraisal cuts. Listings priced on three comps and a
items.text: 03 Defensible pricing stops appraisal cuts. Listings priced on three comps and a guess get appraisal cuts. We defend your contract price with institutional math. When the buyer’s appraiser shows up, I hand them a documented analysis — Sales Comparison, Income Approach, Cost Approach.

items.name: 04 The Military Relocation / PCS math. If you’re an active-duty family facing a
items.text: 04 The Military Relocation / PCS math. If you’re an active-duty family facing a PCS, the first question isn’t — it’s Before listing, we run the rent-vs-sell proforma. how do I sell? should I sell at all? Sometimes the best financial move is to keep the asset. I’ll tell you that upfront.

items.name: 01 Strategy session & the “should you sell?” test. First call, no listing agreem
items.text: 01 Strategy session & the “should you sell?” test. First call, no listing agreement. We talk through your goals, your timeline, your existing mortgage, your tax situation, and what you’d want to do with the proceeds. If you have a 2.75% mortgage and don’t actually need to move, the math might say hold it. If you have $600K of dead equity and a clear next move, the math says go. The honest first question is: should you sell at all? Initial call

items.name: 02 The valuation & prep. An in-person walkthrough at the home, then the three-ap
items.text: 02 The valuation & prep. An in-person walkthrough at the home, then the three-approach analysis. — paint, landscaping, minor fixes, a few targeted upgrades — get done. Overimprovements that wouldn’t return their cost don’t. Staging, architectural photography, drone where the lot tells a story, twilight where the home does. Repairs that actually recover their cost This is where 5–10% of the sale price lives. 1–2 weeks

items.name: 03 Dual-audience marketing launch. Listing goes live with the full package: MLS,
items.text: 03 Dual-audience marketing launch. Listing goes live with the full package: MLS, professional photography, property website, targeted social, broker network outreach, and a coordinated open-house schedule. Lifestyle imagery for families. Hard data, proformas, and development upside for the investor network. If the valuation showed your home appeals to investors or developers — not just families — separate marketing materials go out to each pool. Active listing

items.name: 04 Negotiation & escrow. Offers come in. We evaluate them on price terms — finan
items.text: 04 Negotiation & escrow. Offers come in. We evaluate them on price terms — financing contingency, inspection contingency, close timeline, seller credits, leaseback if you need time to move. Once accepted, I quarterback escrow: appraisal defense, inspection negotiations, title, lender milestones, and the final walkthrough. and The best offer is rarely just the highest number. 30–45 days

items.name: 05 Trade-up or 1031 exchange coordination. Most agents stop at Step 4. If you’re
items.text: 05 Trade-up or 1031 exchange coordination. Most agents stop at Step 4. If you’re redeploying proceeds into income property — duplex, fourplex, or small multifamily — Step 5 is where I run the buy-side in parallel. If the property is investment, not primary, we use a 1031 exchange instead — strict 45-day identification, 180-day close, qualified intermediary holds the funds. Underwriting your next acquisition before the listing agreement. If applicable

items.name: Path A · Entry 12 – One ADU — or a garage conversion. The most popular project f
items.text: Path A · Entry 12 – One ADU — or a garage conversion. The most popular project for first-time builders. Add one detached ADU in the back (typically 600–1,200 sf), or convert your existing garage into a separate unit. Lower cost, smaller footprint, faster timeline. Most owners can fund this with a HELOC or renovation loan — no major capital event required.

items.name: Path B · Core play 24 – Two to four units — then refinance and redeploy. Build 2
items.text: Path B · Core play 24 – Two to four units — then refinance and redeploy. Build 2–4 new units alongside your existing home. Lease them up. Then refinance at the property's dramatically higher appraised value. The cash-out refinance pays off the construction loan and returns most of your original equity. This is the play most of my development clients run.

items.name: Path C · Maximum ~ 10 Up to ~10 units — maximum lot value. For larger lots, mult
items.text: Path C · Maximum ~ 10 Up to ~10 units — maximum lot value. For larger lots, multifamily-zoned lots, lots in Transit Priority Areas, or vacant single-family lots eligible for (effective July 2025 — up to 10 homes by-right, CEQA-exempt, 60-day approval). Bigger team, bigger budget, bigger return — and bigger feasibility burden up front. SB 1123

items.name: · Why this is possible right now CA law Four California housing laws have stacke
items.text: · Why this is possible right now CA law Four California housing laws have stacked up to unlock all of this. Every lot has a different combination available. — California revisits housing laws every legislative cycle. The free lot review tells you what your lot supports today. This legal stack is a window, not a guarantee SB 9 · lot split + 4 units State ADU law · by-right Density Bonus Law SB 1123 · ~10 units by-right

items.name: Approach 01 Sales Sales Comparison. Pull verified recent sales and adjust line-b
items.text: Approach 01 Sales Sales Comparison. Pull verified recent sales and adjust line-by-line for time, location, view, design, condition, and finish. This is the baseline.

items.name: Approach 02 Income Income Approach. What your home would rent for, valued at the
items.text: Approach 02 Income Income Approach. What your home would rent for, valued at the local San Diego market cap rate. This is what an investor would pay for your property as a performing asset.

items.name: Approach 03 Cost Cost Approach. Land value plus what it would cost to rebuild to
items.text: Approach 03 Cost Cost Approach. Land value plus what it would cost to rebuild today, less depreciation. The sanity check.

items.name: Approach 04 HBU Highest-and-Best-Use Premium. The developer’s lens. Added value
items.text: Approach 04 HBU Highest-and-Best-Use Premium. The developer’s lens. Added value if your lot qualifies for SB 9, SB 1123, the State Density Bonus, or ADU stacking. We add this premium to your list price so you capture the equity — not the developer who buys it.
